publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: This paper studies the CMRP developed long base bulk p-i-n diode of different topologies as a displacement damage dose (DDD) sensor for high energy heavy ion fields typical of the galatic cosmic ray (GCR) radiation environment. The investigation attempts to demonstrate that the developed p-i-n diodes response is independent of incident heavy ion type and remains in agreement with the theoretically predicted DDD for various energies. Such sensors will be useful for space missions to predict damage of solar cells and other electronics and implement mitigation measures in time.

articleTitle: MASS-Cube: a CubeSat Compton telescope based on pixelated CdZnTe detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: The Gamma-rays in the MeV range are rich with scientific potential, whereas the sensitivity of telescopes operating in this range is much more worse than neighboring ranges. 3-D position-sensitive semiconductor detectors with high spatial resolution and high energy resolution shed new light on exploring this range. MASS-Cube is a CubeSat Compton telescope using pixelated CdZnTe detectors, based on the successful experiences of GRID CubeSat mission. Simulations and experiments have been done to evaluate the performances. A sub-millimeter position resolution and an energy resolution of ~1% at 662 keV is achieved.

articleTitle: Advanced Photon-Counting Detector Simulator with a Count-Rate-Dependent Mapping Operator and a Pixel-to-Pixel Variation Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Photon-counting detector (PCD)-based computed tomography (CT) imaging improves diagnostic accuracy and lowers radiation exposure, requiring realistic and versatile simulation tools for algorithm development. Existing model-based PCD simulators, however, have limitations in accurately modeling PCD outputs, such as missing pixel-to-pixel variations and unidentified mismatches between ideal models and actual measurements. The study aimed to develop an advanced PCD-based CT simulator that overcomes these limitations in existing simulators. Our simulator is based on the PCD output model that was built upon the cascaded model. To develop an advanced PCD simulator, we modified and generalized the previously established condition-specific functions, creating a count-rate-dependent energy mapping operator and a pixel-to-pixel variation generator. These components were then incorporated into the existing model. To evaluate the simulator's performance, we compared its outputs with CdZnTe-based PCD measurements and analyzed the effects of varying several tunable parameters on spectrum outputs and pixel-to-pixel variations. Comparison of the simulator outputs with the measurements showed remarkable agreement for a wide range of incident count-rates. The mean absolute percentage error for all energy bins was 4.67 %, indicating effective reproduction of the physical PCD measurements. Adjusting the major parameters visually showed their spectral distortion effects due to pulse pileup and charge sharing. This adjustment also allowed us to easily modulate or balance the pixel-to-pixel variations across energy bins, indicating effective control of the output spectrum and these variations. Our study successfully developed an advanced PCD simulator that offers a more accurate representation of the inherent detector behavior. The proposed simulator is a valuable tool for developing and evaluating new algorithms and techniques for PCD-based CT imaging.

articleTitle: 3D-Flow, 3D-CBS and TB-CAD inventions create a revolutionary paradigm change in the practice of medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: To solve the most deadly (over 10 million lives/year) and costly (over $1.5 Trillion/year) disease, it is necessary to invite all people claiming to have a solution to cancer to present their theory/calculations/proposals, summarized in a table where the lives and costs saved each year are estimated for the next 30 years, to defend their claims in a public meeting with other proposers and experts in the field and provide references to any proposal superior to the 3D-Flow, 3D-CBS and TB-CAD inventions which create a revolutionary paradigm change in the practice of medicine. The 3D-Flow architecture breaks the speed barrier in real-time applications and accurately captures all possible valid signals filtered from radiation at the lowest cost per valid signal captured. The 3D-CBS (3-D Complete Body Screening) is a cost-effective hardware tool for early detection of diseases, including cancer, that captures simultaneously all possible signals from transmitted (CT) and emitted (PET) photons (radiation) from the radioisotope (tracer) associated with proteins, nutrient molecules, etc. of all organs, recognizing anomaly activity in biological processes in clusters (diseases or tumors) of less than 100 body cells at €200 per screening test, requiring very low radiation. In comparison, current CT, MRI, Mammogram, Ultrasound, can only detect large clusters (diseases or tumors) from 1,000,000 body cells (the size of a 1mm tumor), or one billion cells/1cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> by measuring differences in tissue density which is less efficient than the 3D-CBS measuring biophysiology. TB-CAD (Total-Body Computer-Aided Diagnosis) is a powerful software tool that brings to fruition the advantages of the two previous inventions and allows the correlation of abnormal biological processes in different parts of the body to understand biophysiological functioning, prevent diseases, and improve diagnosis, prognosis, and effective monitoring of treatments, ensuring the removal of cancerous or diseased cells.

articleTitle: Pitfall in the Implementation of Acollinearity in PET Monte Carlo Simulation Softwares
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Acollinearity of annihilation photons is a source of spatial blur in PET imaging that increases with the scanner radius. It was demonstrated that acollinearity follows a Gaussian distribution. This statement can refer to two concepts: the amplitude of the acollinearity angle or the angular deviation of the annihilation photons relative to the collinear case. Since the former is the partial integral of the latter, an error of interpretation could have significant repercussions. Previous works that have studied the effect of acollinearity in PET imaging have made the assumption that the angular deviation is Gaussian, which is in agreement with experimental studies. However, we show that in GATE, a PET simulation software, acollinearity is simulated as the former. This not only changes the shape of the spatial blur induced in the image space but also significantly reduces its effect on spatial resolution, e.g., from 2.1 mm FWHM to 0.4 mm FWHM for a PET scanner ≈ 80 cm in diameter. This underestimation is shared with other PET simulation softwares. Results obtained with these simulators would underestimate, sometimes severely, the blur induced by acollinearity. We propose an approach to simulate acollinearity that follows the latter interpretation and show that it would be adequate for PET imaging.

articleTitle: The Cadmium Zinc Telluride (CZT) Polarimeter onboard the XL-Calibur Hard X-ray Telescope Mission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: XL-Calibur is a balloon-borne hard X-ray (15-80 keV) polarimetry mission funded by NASA, optimized to examine the linear polarization of emission from black hole, neutron star, and supernova systems. These measurements will help test the limits of astrophysical and fundamental physics theories.Incoming X-ray photons are focused onto a beryllium scattering rod, surrounded by seventeen 2 x 2 x 0.1 cm^3 Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) detectors. CZT is a key choice for hard X-ray detection without resorting to cryogenic cooling. The 64 pixels of each CZT detector are read-out with ASICs designed by the Naval Research Laboratory.In this presentation, I will discuss the design of our scalable CZT detector system. After presenting results on the detection efficiency and energy resolution of the CZT detectors from Kromek and Redlen, I will comment on the performance of the polarimeter as a whole in the presence of ASIC-ASIC cross-talk.I will furthermore report on the in-flight performance of the polarimeter on the previous stratospheric balloon flights from McMurdo, Antarctica (2018-2019) and Esrange, Sweden (2022). We plan to fly the polarimeter again in 2024 from Esrange and in 2026-2027 from McMurdo.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Impact of Optical Crosstalk for a Scintillator Based TOF-CT Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) has witnessed remarkable advancements in the last decade, particularly in the reduction of X-ray exposure, while maintaining high-quality images. A novel concept that enhances contrast-to-noise ratio substitutes the anti-scatter grid with a photon filtering method based on time of flight (ToF). The ToF-CT detector design includes an array of small, optically isolated scintillator crystals, each connected to an independent photosensor, to measure the ToF information of individual X-ray photons. However, the interaction of photons produced by an X-ray with a scintillator crystal can result in the emission of visible light beyond the crystal boundaries, leading to signal contamination and reduced performance through inter-crystal crosstalk. As the crystals become narrower for better spatial resolution, the probability of optical crosstalk is expected to increase. To assess the impact of inter-crystal crosstalk on the sensitivity and spatial resolution of ToF-CT detectors, we conducted a Monte Carlo simulation of scintillation events in the detector and evaluated several crosstalk metrics for various configurations of LYSO crystals connected to SiPM arrays. For a spherical collimated source located in the middle of a central scintillation detector measuring 1x1x2.5 mm3 and a lower energy threshold of 20 keV, the probability of optical crosstalk for one X-ray was found to be 0.12%. These findings indicate that ignoring crosstalk signals can reduce tomograph sensitivity using these detectors, along with a 7% decrease in energy resolution.

articleTitle: Fast neutron spectrometry using chemically modified plastic scintillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: In the nuclear safety and radiation protection context, the identification of neutron sources and the knowledge of neutron dose rate, which require an accurate measurement of the energy spectrum, are needed. This study highlights the potential of chemically modified plastic scintillators as a neutron spectrometer. These detectors offer the possibility to determine the energy spectrum of a neutron source from a measured pulse height spectrum by using a deconvolution method. In our work, we use a homemade plastic scintillator able to discriminate fast neutrons from gamma rays. The MLEM (Maximum Likelihood Expectation Maximization) algorithm has been selected for the neutron spectrum deconvolution method. In a first time, we used the neutron beam available in the Amande facility to determine the light response function of the detector. In a second time, we employed this parameter for optimizing the MCNP6.2 simulated response function. The neutron spectra of Cf-252 and AmBe, which are unfolded using experimental data, show an excellent agreement with their reference spectra for neutron energies above 2 MeV.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Experimental Data into a MLEM Reconstruction Algorithm for Fast Neutron Emission Tomography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: A primary part of nuclear nonproliferation and nuclear security principles involves verification of spent fuel to ensure no material diversion has occurred. As a result, various verification technologies have been developed to detect when irradiated fuel pins have gone outside of regulatory control. One proposed method of spent nuclear fuel verification includes using a fast neutron emission tomography system for spent nuclear fuel. This system would allow for imaging of individual fuel pins and quantifications of neutron source strength. A proof-of concept fast neutron emission tomography system for verification of spent nuclear fuel was constructed at ORNL. An analytic neutron response model used in MLEM reconstructions was created based on the system’s geometry and results from MCNP simulations. In order to ensure accurate reconstructions of spent fuel, a series of measurements were performed to characterize the as-built imager. Results from this data were incorporated into the analytic neutron response model to match the analytic responses to the real response of the system. Characterization measurements were made to improve neutron detector efficiency values, collimator penetration of neutrons, and collimator slit scattering values. Using the data collected, these values were incorporated into the analytic response model and new reconstructions of mock fuel pins were created. The end goal is to have a neutron response model which accurately depicts the as-built system’s response and produces accurate reconstructions of whole spent fuel assemblies.

articleTitle: A Software-Scalable Analog-to-Digital Converter for Particle Detectors in 28nm bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: New discoveries in particle physics put an ever-increasing demand on the installed electronics in detector experiments. Currently used process technologies for integrated electronics, as 65nm and larger, are reaching their limits of resolution over power consumption and integration factor. The consequential progression to a smaller process technology comes with increased cost and design complexity resulting in a higher impact on the overall success of a project. The currently discussed way out of this predicament is concentrating cost and effort in fewer, more generic solutions covering a wider range of applications. A first prototype of a software-scalable Analog-to-Digital converter manufactured in a 28nm bulk CMOS process technology is presented, which is part of a generic frontend solution concept. It incorporates a low-power mode with 8 bit of resolution, a maximum sample rate of 480 MSPS, and a power consumption of 1.62 mW. When higher resolution is needed, a high-precision mode can be used with a resolution of 11 bit, a maximum sample rate of 350 MSPS and a power consumption of 5.6 mW. The complete software-scalable Analog-to-Digital converter takes 0.029 mm² of chip area. Overall, the first chip is 1 mm² in size. It includes two channels, a high-speed parallel communication interface, a clock buffer and memory for 8168 Analog-to-Digital converter samples.

articleTitle: Performance prediction of a high-performance whole-body human PET scanner by simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: High-performance whole-body human PET scanners with excellent spatial resolution (< 2.5 mm) can potentially increase information content in the images for more accurate diagnosis. However, existing whole-body scanners have limited spatial resolution of ~3 mm or greater. This study proposes a high-performance PET scanner to address this need and predicted its performance by Monte Carlo simulation. The proposed PET scanner has 8 detector rings, and each ring consists of 32 dual-ended readout detectors. Each detector has two SiPM arrays coupled to both ends of a 32 × 32 array of 2.1 × 2.1 × 20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> LYSOs. The pitch size of the LYSO arrays is 2.2 mm. This scanner has a ring diameter of 780 mm and an axial length of 624.8 mm. The proposed scanner was simulated using GATE (v8.2), and the images were reconstructed using a TOF list-mode OSEM algorithm with image-space point spread function. Our simulation shows that radial spatial resolutions at the axial center with using DOI were 1.4, 1.5 and 1.7 mm for the radial offsets of 1, 10, and 20 cm, respectively. The corresponding radial resolution without using DOI information are 1.5, 3.1 and 6.2 mm. The sensitivity is 69 cps/kBq at the center of the scanner. The Derenzo phantom images show that 1.6-mm rods are visually resolved over the entire FOV given the DOI used, and better digital Hoffman brain phantom images were obtained using the DOI information compared to without using the DOI. The proposed design can be extended in the axial direction to form a total-body PET system.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a High-Sensitivity Organ-Targeted Positron Emission Tomography (PET) System for Small Lesion Detection and Quantitative Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: In this study, we evaluate the imaging performance of the Radialis PET camera, a high-sensitivity organ-targeted Positron Emission Tomography (PET) system, using standardized and custom tests previously used for Positron Emission Mammography (PEM) systems. We assess the imaging characteristics related to standardized uptake value (SUV) and detectability of small lesions, including spatial resolution, linearity, uniformity, and recovery coefficients. In-plane spatial resolution of 2.3 mm ± 0.1 mm, spatial accuracy of 0.1 mm, and uniformity measured with flood field and NEMA NU-4 phantom of 11.7% and 8.3%, respectively are reported. Recovery coefficients were measured to be 0.21 for the 1 mm hot rod and up to 0.89 for the 5 mm hot rod of NEMA NU-4 phantom, indicating the ability of Radialis PET camera to accurately reconstruct activity in tumors as small as 5 mm.Radialis PET camera provides an improved contrast recovery and spill-over ratio compared to other organ-dedicated PET systems with similar spatial resolution. We relate this improvement to optimized count rate performance and image reconstruction workflow. Presented clinical images demonstrate the imaging capabilities of the system under different conditions, such as reduced 2-[fluorine-18]-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose (18F-FDG) activity and time-delayed acquisitions. SUV measurements in clinical images show that the Radialis PET camera can provide accurate quantitative assessment for different types of cancer, including invasive lobular carcinoma with low metabolic activity.Due to the improved accuracy of tumor activity evaluation, the Radialis PET camera may be well-suited for emerging clinical applications, such as image-guided assessment of response to neoadjuvant systemic treatment (NST) in lesions smaller than 2 cm. The study also highlights the importance of recovery coefficient as a primary performance metric when targeting PET systems for accurate lesion size and radiotracer uptake assessment.

articleTitle: Study of ToF Capabilities in PET Detector Array Modules Designed for High Spatial Resolution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Time-of-flight (ToF) implementations on positron emission tomography (PET) are a promising technology that has become increasingly popular in the field since its introduction improves image quality by reducing noise and increasing contrast, which are critical benefits when it comes to analyzing highly detailed anatomical structures. In this work the implementation of ToF is studied for high resolution PET detector array modules. This system uses a 25 x 6 lutetium-yttrium oxyorthosilicate (LYSO) crystal array coupled to array of the same size of 1 x 1 mm silicon photmultipliers (SiPM), This array is managed by a PETsys TOFPET2 ASIC. The SiPM were fed with a pre-breakdown voltage of 22 V, a break-down voltage of 25 V and an over-voltage of 5V. We evaluated the energy resolution and coincidence resolving time (CRT). We obtained an energy resolution of 19.6 % full width at half maximum (FWHM) and a CRT of 531.8 ps FWHM. While these results are not state-of-the-art yet, further refinement of these results will be done to extract the system's full potential.

articleTitle: Researchand Development Volume Detection System for Graphite and Carbon ComponentsBased on Electron Linear Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: The Institute of Nuclear and New Energy Technology (INET) has developed a spiral CT detection system for small graphite and carbon components. The system uses 60Co as a radiation source, which provides good stability and can detect large quantities of graphite and carbon components over an extended period. However, it cannot meet the detection requirements of large-sized components. This paper is based on the X-ray spectrum and attenuation coefficient of graphite and carbon components, as well as the optimization of the layout parameters of the system, to design a detection system based on a 9 MeV electron linear accelerator. This system can preliminarily meet the volume detection needs of large-sized graphite and carbon components in the reactor core, in the range of 700 mm-1000 mm. The results show that the accelerator detection system can effectively penetrate large graphite components, and theoretically can achieve a defect detection requirement of 1mm according to the design of the detector. The accelerator system and the isotope source system can complement each other well.

articleTitle: Low-dose PET Image Reconstruction Based on Cascaded Fully Connected Layers and U-shaped Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Reducing the tracer dose in Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging can decrease the radiation risk for patients and the cost of the examination. However, this can lead to the reconstructed images having severe noise. In this paper, we propose a neural network that can directly reconstruct low-count sinograms into PET images. The proposed network consists of two parts: the domain transform part and the U-shaped network part. The domain transform part uses the weighted vector and fully conntected layers to learn the domain tranformation for each image patch. The whole PET image is divided into 4×4 patche array with size of 32×32. The U-shaped network then synthesizes the features among all image patches and generate the final reconstructed PET image. The proposed network improves the quality of reconstructed images while avoiding iterative reconstruction, thereby reducing time consumption. Compared to ordered subset expectation maximization (OSEM) with a post-Gaussian filter and the state-of-the-art convolutional neural network, the structural similarity can be improved to 0.96 and the peak signal-to-noise ratio to 31.34 dB, while consuming only 16% and 55% of the time.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Multi-Organ Extraction and Geometric Modeling for Radiotherapy Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Radiation simulations have been widely used in high energy physics, nuclear physics, accelerator physics, medical science, and space science. Geant4 is one of the powerful radiation simulation toolkits for Monte Carlo radiation simulations. It simulates passages of particles through matter and generates physical quantities in detectors, equipment, or a human body. We have been developing an AI-assisted RoI extraction and DVH calculation tool, gRovai. gRovai uses NVIDIA Clara Holoscan to extract a tumor or organ region from a DICOM image dataset using AI. gRovai has been implemented functions to extract regions of organs and tumors in human body images such as a DICOM dataset, edit the extracted regions to correct them manually, and construct and visualize a three-dimensional geometric model of radiotherapy simulation. The geometric model of a human body for radiotherapy simulation is constructed with tetrahedral meshes for higher precision and fast simulation. gRovai is going to be available freely as standalone software.

articleTitle: A Prompt Gamma-ray Detection Module for Imaging, Timing and Spectroscopy in Hadrontherapy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: We present a gamma-ray detection module consisting of a 8×8 pixelated LYSO scintillator coupled with a 64-SiPM array, four custom 16-channel SITH ASICs and a FPGA-based DAQ system providing a real-time measurement of the gamma-ray hit position, energy and time-of-arrival through 64 TDCs implemented in FPGA. The detector and readout electronics have been specifically designed and optimized for the prompt gamma (PG) imaging application used for range monitoring in hadrontherapy and thus feature a high countrate capability (up to 0.6 Mcps per channel), a large dynamic range of ~ 90 dB (for reading energies up to 8 MeV deposited in a single crystal pixel) and the possibility of scattering correction through time coincidence measurement. We report the design of the 64-channel detection module electronics, along with a preliminary experimental measurements of a first 16-channel prototype of the system in terms of energy and timing performance. The timestamp difference distribution obtained by pulsing two TDC channels shows a FWHM of 110 ps.

articleTitle: Study on conditioning effect of TlBr semiconductor detectors with gold electrodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Thallium bromide (TlBr) is a compound semiconductor attractive for gamma-ray spectrometers with high detection efficiency. Owing to recent detector developments, TlBr detectors have shown excellent energy resolution. One of the recent topics of TlBr detector developments is a long-term stability or the polarization effect. There are two sides to this issue: the conditioning and degradation effects of the detector performance. Although the degradation effect can be explained as a result of the chemical reaction or deterioration of an electrode material, there is no detail discussion on an origin of the conditioning effect. In this paper, to discuss a mechanism of the conditioning effect, we evaluate temporal changes of the charge collection efficiency or mobility-lifetime product under continuously applying voltage to the TlBr detector. Consequently, we concluded that the mobility-lifetime product of the holes is improved by the conditioning operation.

articleTitle: Auto Single Respiratory Gate by Deep Data Driven Gating for PET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Data driven respiratory gating is sometimes used in positron emission tomography (PET) imaging, in order to reduce respiratory motion blur without requiring external devices. Once the respiratory motion is estimated, the PET data may be binned and reconstructed into multiple gates (for visualizing the motion) or a single gate (for a single, motion-reduced image). In a common use case, the single gate is selected to align with the quiescent phase around end-expiration; however, due to the irregular respiratory motion, the quiescent phase approach may not be optimal. In this study, we proposed a data-driven approach using an autoencoder (AE) network, unsupervised feature identification and latent-feature clustering in order to generate a single-frame image, which is referred to as auto single quiescent gating method. A moving IEC phantom and two FDG-PET patients data were acquired to evaluated the proposed gating method. We compared the proposed method with non-gated and conventional quiescent phase gating method. Image quality was evaluated by comparing contrast recovery coefficient for the phantom data and tumor volume and intensity for the patient data. Both phantom data and clinical patient data showed its superior ability to reduce motion blur and improve tumor quantification.

articleTitle: Performance of NEMA characteristics of Modular J-PET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: The Modular J-PET scanner, developed by the J-PET collaboration, is a new prototype PET scanner developed based on axially arranged plastic scintillators as a large axial field of view (50cm) affordable tomograph. In this study, the performance characteristics of the scanner were evaluated according to NEMA NU2-2018 standards using Monte Carlo simulation. In order to ensure the selection of true coincidence events, certain criteria were established. Specifically, each photon emitting from a single annihilation must deposit at least 200 keV within 4 ns of a coincidence time window. The preliminary results showed that the sensitivity profile peak was 4 cps/kBq at the center of the detector, While the scatter fraction was estimated to be 39% using the single slice rebinning algorithm. Spatial resolution was estimated around 4.5 mm in the radial and tangential direction and 18 mm in the axial direction.

articleTitle: Ultra-low Dark Current and Highly Sensitive X-ray Detection using Cu-doped Cs3Bi2Br9 Perovskite Single Crystals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)

A sensitivity of 264 μC ${\text{G}}{{\text{y}}_{{\text{air}}}}^{ - 1}{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^{ - 2}}$ was achieved under irradiation of 30 kV X-ray and applied electric field of 40 Vmm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. articleTitle: Compton imaging using high resolution scintillation detectors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: A prototype Compton camera is built by using an ultra-high spatial resolution scatter detector consisting of a gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) scintillator array with a crystal size of 0.35×0.35×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> read out by a SiPM array and a high 3D spatial resolution absorb detector consisting of an lutetium yttrium orthosilicate (LYSO) scintillator array with a crystal size of 1×1×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> dual-ended read out by SiPM arrays. A novel image reconstruction algorithm that combines a simple back-projection method and a MLEM method was also developed and tested by using Monte Carlo simulation data. The performance of the detectors were measured. The results showed that all but the edge crystals can be clearly resolved and average energy resolutions of 13.5% and 19.1% were achieved for the two detectors. In the next step, point source and phantom data will be acquired using the prototype Compton camera. The spatial resolution, sensitivity and image performance of the prototype Compton camera will be evaluated.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Generative Vision Transformer for Attenuation and Scatter Correction in Brain PET
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Attenuation correction is essential for accurate PET images, as it corrects for photon loss due to scatter or absorption in tissue, which can reduce PET signal intensity by up to 90%. Deep Learning methods have been proposed to generate pseudo-CT images from MR for AC in PET. Despite their potential, generating pseudo-CT images from MRI data remains a challenge due to issues such as poor image quality, limited tissue heterogeneity, patient-specific anatomical variations, and pathologies, as well as time-consuming processing. We present a novel generative deep learning approach to obtain attenuation and scatter-corrected (ASC) PET images directly from non-attenuation and non-scatter-corrected (NASC) images. Retrospective 18Ffluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) full-body PET/CT and PET/MR images from 36 subjects were collected and analyzed. We designed and trained a conditional generative vision transformer adversarial network (ViT-GAN) capable of handling single and multi-modal data to map NASC images to pixel-wise continuously valued ASC PET images. The ViT-GAN framework resulted in more accurately corrected PET images, closer to the ground truth, when using the multi-modal (NASC+ MR Dixon Fat and Water) data as a multi-channel input compared to just using a single modality (NASC) as a single input channel. The average peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index for the multi-modal ViT-GAN input were 38 and 0.97 versus 36 and 0.955 for the single-modality input, respectively. ViT-GAN was demonstrated to be a promising approach for direct attenuation and scatter correction of brain PET images with clinically acceptable error levels. It has the potential to perform accurate attenuation correction on standalone PET or PET/MRI systems.

articleTitle: Quantitative CT-less PET Imaging with Energy-based Scatter Estimations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: There has been an increasing interest in low-dose PET scans, in particular after the introduction of long-axial field-of-view PET/CT scanners. Performing a CT scan in studies where CT is merely done for the attenuation and scatter correction of PET data undermines the true low-dose premise of such PET studies. We have shown in the past that one can potentially use the background radiation from lutetium in long-axial field-of-view PET scanners with lutetium-based scintillators to reconstruct an estimate of attenuation maps which can then be improved in a joint reconstruction algorithm such as maximum likelihood reconstruction of activity and attenuation (MLAA). However, the lack of an accurate scatter estimates in such algorithms can lead to a bias and quantitative inaccuracies in the reconstructed PET images. In this work, we propose and evaluate the use of an energy-based scatter estimation algorithm in CT-less reconstruction for a long-axial field-of-view PET/CT scanner. Using the data from a NEMA NU-2 image quality phantom scan on a Biograph Vision Quadra PET/CT scanner (Siemens Healthineers), reconstructed images with and without the use CT and with and without the use of energy-based scatter estimates are shown. The results suggest that images reconstructed with CT-based correction and standard ordered-subset expectation maximization reconstructions match well with CT-less reconstructions and energy-based scatter. In conclusions, the use of an energy-based scatter estimation algorithm is a promising solution to the issue of scatter in CT-less reconstruction methods.

articleTitle: The performance research and optimization of the Beam Shaping Assembly (BSA) used for BNCT based on the cyclotron
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Cancer has become one of the important factors threatening human life and health, and methods for treating cancer are constantly being studied and explored. It is an urgent demand in the healthcare to treat cancer by rays. Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) is given increasing amount of attention due to its ability of selective cancer cell killing. The BNCT based on the 18 MeV/1 mA cyclotron is researched. To improve the flux of the epithermal neutrons, simultaneously reducing fast neutron dose and photon dose as much as possible, this paper studies the generation and transport of neutrons in the Beam Shaping Assembly (BSA) of the BNCT. An optimized BSA structure is designed. Be is chosen as the target to produce neutron by <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>Be(p,n)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>B reaction. The BSA consists of Pb as neutron multiplier and reflector, TiF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Al as moderators, Ni as filter, B-Poly as shield and Bi as collimator. The neutron yield can achieved 5.25×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> n/s. The epithermal neutron flux is 2.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> n/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s, with the fast neutron dose of 6.61×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> Gy•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per epithermal neutron and the photon dose of 2.24×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> Gy•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per epithermal neutron.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Fast Neutron Imaging System Based on Associated Alpha Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: A fast neutron imaging system based on the associated alpha technique has been developed by our group. It consists of a D-T neutron generator with an associated alpha detector, a neutron-block detector array, a sample station, a multi-channel data acquisition system. The associated particle neutron generator independently developed by our group can produce a 14 MeV neutron flux of 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> n/s with a variation of less than 6%. The integrated associated alpha detector is made out of a YAP:Ce scintillator read out by a position sensitive photomultiplier. The test results with an 241Am alpha source show that it has a spatial resolution of better than 2 mm and a timing resolution of about 432 ps. The sample station can move tested samples up and down with a resolution of 0.1 mm, and rotate samples with an angular resolution of 0.1 degree. The neutron block detector array consists of 3X3 individual neutron block detectors. Each of them is made out of 10X10 EJ200 plastic scintillators which are read out by an array of 10X10 6mmX6mm Sensl C-series SiPMs.In addition, the whole system has been modeled using Geant4 program and 36 projections of highly enriched uranium (HEU) and polyethylene samples were simulated at 10° intervals. With the FDK and POCS-TVM algorithms, the simulated sample can be reconstructed in 5.6s and 6.7min. For FDK and POCS-TVM algorithms, the SNRs of images are: 3.7 and 5.2, respectively; and the CNRs of images are 1.6 and 2.7, respectively. Meanwhile, the reconstruction time of POCS-TVM algorithm can be decreased from 6.7min to 1.6min after the use of GPU acceleration. The experimental tests on different samples have been carried out and the results will be reported at this meeting.

articleTitle: Development and Construction of a Cost-effective PET-like Detector System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: In this paper, a cost-effective PET-like detector system is presented. The innovative system consisting of 88 plastic scintillators of 1 m length and customized silicon photomultiplier arrays is developed to reduce the overall cost of otherwise very expensive commercial PET scanners. Fully assembled, it spans a volume of about 0.5 x 0.5 x 1 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Due to the two-sided readout of the scintillator bars, the detector system provides bulk-internal information within large, dense, and even optically opaque systems by combining positron emission particle tracking with time-of-flight measurements. With this capability, it becomes very interesting for many large-scale industrial processes, such as waste incineration or the treatment of bulk solids in process, chemical, pharmaceutical, and food industry. Results of a prototype setup will be presented.

articleTitle: Total body PET attenuation correction based on low dose CT and non-attenuation-corrected PET images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: A total-body PET/CT scanner with a long axial field of view offers much sensitivity for clinical imaging and research. However, it may lead to more radiation exposure for the whole body rather than a single-site examination. In particular, more X-ray exposure is needed to cover the whole body instead of a single site as in common CT, which accounts for the major dose of radiation. Considering this motivation, we explored a dual dose reduction strategy to apply low-dose CT and low-dose PET scanning protocols on a total body system for PET attenuation correction. To conduct this dose reduction task, we proposed a deep learning method implemented with a novel network model equipped with several spatial position alignment modules, where multiscale feature information of low-dose CT images and low-dose NAC PET are fused and ultimately predict normal-dose PET images. Quantitative measurement metrics are used to evaluate the performance, and the experimental results prove the effectiveness of the proposed methods. Moreover, we found that 1.0% NAC PET could provide excellent identification of lesions, and 25% NAC PET scanning data generated more texture details than the ground truth. In the future, further research on dose reduction should be explored for total body PET/CT systems.

articleTitle: Estimated random rate for an intraoperative use of the forceps-type coincidence detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: In surgical cancer treatment, extensive lymph node (LN) dissection has been noted as being related to postoperative complications. On the other hand, it has also been reported that approximately 95% of the resected LNs in esophagectomy were not metastases. Therefore, optimization of LN dissection with intraoperative LN diagnosis is expected to reduce postoperative complications. As a biomarker for LNs metastasis, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose (FDG) provides a high diagnostic performance in positron emission tomography (PET). To realize intraoperative FDG-PET measurement for individual LNs, we have proposed a forceps-type coincidence detector, which consists of a pair of small scintillation detectors mounted on the head of a forceps to detect an annihilation-radiation pair. The proposed device can quantify activity concentration in a small area between the heads of its forceps. However, most of the injected FDG spreads over organs outside of the field-of-detection of the device, which may increase the random rate, and statistical error of the LN activity measurement should be carefully assessed with a practical short data acquisition time such as 30 s. In this research, we simulated LN diagnosis with the proposed forceps-type coincidence detector (with BGO crystals) by modeling an actual FDG distribution in each organ. With a clinically typical injection dose of FDG and at the time of two half-lives of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>F passing, the random fraction was less than 30% and the statistical error was less than 5 %, which supported the feasibility of in-vivo use of our forceps-type coincidence detector currently under development.

articleTitle: Time-Resolved Digital Data Processing Enhancements in Neutron Active Interrogation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: Active interrogation signatures of contraband and special nuclear material are often relatively weak, requiring the use of long measurement times and high radiation doses from the interrogating source. We are exploring new digital pulse processing techniques for active neutron interrogation to enhance the detection of concealed contraband and special nuclear material with a focus on prompt gamma-ray signatures for drug and explosive detection and fast neutron detection for special nuclear material. The new detection systems make use of digital data acquisition from inorganic and organic scintillators, the time structure of deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fast neutron generator interrogation sources to improve signal-to-backgroud ratios, and a reconfigurable water-based fast neutron collimation system to reduce activation backgrounds. We characterized the fast neutron time profile of the Thermo Scientific P211 DT neutron generator using organic scintillators and a gamma-blind He-4 fast neutron detector. We discuss the spectra and time profiles from active interrogation measurements performed with contraband simulants and inorganic scintillators, including fast inorganic scintillators such as LaBr3. We additionally applied maximum likelihood estimation maximization-based spectral reconstruction with organic scintillators to detect prompt gamma-ray signatures from carbon and nitrogen-rich objects that may allow for the measurement of sample stoichiometry to distinguish contraband from benign samples. Based on these methods, combined spectro-temporal analysis is being developed for detecting shielded contraband with improved sensitivity.

articleTitle: Impact of detector parameters on the imaging performance of a dedicated brain PET scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: High performance brain scanners suitable for accurate and precise measurement of uptake in small regions of the brain require high spatial resolution (1.5-2mm) and effective sensitivity. While small cross-section crystals are needed to achieve high spatial resolution, effective sensitivity requires long crystals and good TOF resolution. In addition, depending on crystal length some level of depth-of-interaction (DOI) capability may also be needed to reduce parallax error. However, long crystals with DOI capability typically degrade TOF resolution. Hence, brain system development normally involves a trade-off between crystal cross-section, crystal length, DOI, and TOF resolution. The focus of this work is to use Monte Carlo simulations and task-based metrics to evaluate these trade-offs in detector design to better guide a new brain system development. Fixing the crystal cross section at 1.6 mm x 1.6 mm, we simulated different LSO crystal thickness (10 mm, 15 mm, and 20 mm), number of DOI layers (1, 2, and 4), and DOI layer assignment accuracy (100% and 80%). Spatial resolution was evaluated as 3-dimensional Full Width of Half Maximum (FWHM) of point sources reconstructed with a list-mode TOF OSEM algorithm. A brain-size phantom was also studied for imaging evaluation. For crystal thickness, we found that 10 mm LSO without DOI performance system performs better than a 20 mm LSO with 2-layer 100% accuracy DOI capability system. Further evaluations using smaller crystal cross-sections and varying TOF resolution will be performed to benchmark not only spatial resolution. In addition, the combined impact of all the detector design parameters on the accuracy and precision of uptake measurement in small structure within the brain and discrimination of small brain structures using a detectability metric will also be evaluated.

articleTitle: Timing Neural Network Implementation in Monolithic PET detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: In Time-Of-Flight Positron Emission Tomography, enhancing coincidence time resolution (CTR) and sensitivity is essential for increasing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). While monolithic detectors have no spatial resolution restrictions, achieving excellent CTR continues to be challenging. Previous studies have employed machine learning techniques to improve CTR). In this work, we investigate the application of neural networks to predict the CTR using only experimental data and analog SiPMs between a monolithic PET detector and a pixelated reference detector. Traditional CTR estimation methods are subject to noise and uncertainty-causing factors, making neural networks a more accurate and reliable approach. Our results show that machine learning algorithms can improve timing resolution in monolithic crystals by decreasing CTR by 200%. Machine learning techniques in data processing have shown significant improvements in position estimation and are beginning to show promise in the timing domain. These findings highlight the potential advantages of incorporating machine learning techniques into PET data processing for improved image quality and SNR gain.

articleTitle: Timing performance of FBK SiPM NUV-HD-MT technology using LYSO:Ce:Ca crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: The need to push the timing performances to the limit finds breeding ground in several fields from high energy physics to biomedical applications such as Time of Flight Positron Emission Tomography (ToF-PET). In the last years, excellent results have been achieved thanks to the improvement of the scintillator crystal materials, the electronics readout and the detector development. In this context, SiPM Coincidence Time Resolution (CTR) is a key parameter in order to assess the device timing performance. In this work we will present the CTR of the recently introduced FBK NUV-HD-MT Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) technology. Thanks to the addition of the optically insulating material inside the trenches, FBK NUV-HDMT devices show an extremely low CrossTalk (CT) of about ≃ 5% at 47.5V (≃ 15V excess bias). The Photon Detection Efficiency (PDE) reaches the ≃ 65% at the same excess bias at 420nm. The CTR was measured using a 4mm × 4mm SiPM to match the 3mm × 3mm × 5mm LYSO:Ce:Ca crystal and comparing different microcell sizes. By using a standard readout electronics we achieved a CTR of ~ 95ps FWHM for all the devices thanks to the extremely low CT of the technology that allows to push the voltage bias to high values. We also compare the CTR between the SiPM version with a metal mask outside the active area (capacitive coupling) and the SiPM without it in order to asses the role of the masking in the timing performance, to discuss about limitations and further improvements.
